page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ebmr7.32xlarge is an ECS Bare Metal instance configured for memory-intensive enterprise workloads. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the system provides 128 dedicated vCPUs powered by Intel Xeon 8369B processors running at a clock speed of 2.9 GHz. System memory totals 1024.0 GB, establishing an allocation ratio of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU core. The platform operates on the KVM hypervisor framework.

Hardware specifications do not include bundled local storage or integrated GPU accelerators, requiring external network-attached block devices for storage needs. To support distributed data transmission and remote disk operations, the instance features a baseline network bandwidth of 64 Gbps. Complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not included.

The 1:8 compute-to-memory ratio provides resource density that benefits workloads requiring extensive active memory without the overhead of shared hypervisor contention. Cost efficiency stems from this density, allowing single-node consolidation for large datasets instead of maintaining multiple distributed nodes. Tradeoffs include total reliance on network throughput for I/O operations due to the absence of local NVMe disks. The instance is suitable for in-memory databases, distributed caching layers, large-scale enterprise resource planning (ERP) platforms, and memory-bound analytics pipelines.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ebmr7.32xlarge is an ECS Bare Metal server designed for high-capacity, memory-intensive computing. Powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8369B processor operating at 2.9 GHz, the server provides 128 dedicated vCPUs alongside 1024.0 GB of RAM, establishing an 8.0 GB per core distribution. The instance does not bundle local disk storage or hardware GPU accelerators, necessitating remote network block storage to satisfy persistent data requirements. Networking performance is supported by a 64 Gbps baseline throughput under KVM virtualization. With substantial dedicated compute resources coupled to a dense 1:8 memory footprint, the ecs.ebmr7.32xlarge provides strong resource density for consolidating large-scale workloads without local storage dependencies. This hardware profile is appropriate for in-memory databases, enterprise caching infrastructures, real-time data processing, and intensive memory-bound workloads.
